rationales: Robert Hooke described cells, not the nucleus.
Laveran discovered the malaria parasite, not the nucleus.
Robert Brown discovered the cell nucleus in 1831.
Louis Pasteur made important contributions to microbiology, not the discovery of the nucleus.
Anopheles mosquitoes are the main vectors of human malaria, not sparrow malaria.
Dengue is a disease, not a mosquito vector.
Aedes mosquitoes transmit diseases such as dengue, not sparrow malaria.
Culex mosquitoes transmit avian malaria to sparrows.
Cell membranes are mainly composed of proteins and lipids.
Cholesterol is present in many membranes but is not their main composition by itself.
Lignin is a substance found in plant cell walls, not a main membrane component.
Chitin is found in fungal cell walls and arthropod exoskeletons, not cell membranes.
Margulis and Schwartz did not introduce the five-kingdom classification.
Torn Efort is not the scientist credited with introducing the five-kingdom classification.
Robert Whittaker introduced the five-kingdom classification.
Ernst Haeckel proposed a three-kingdom classification, not the five-kingdom system.
Goitre is commonly caused by iodine deficiency.
Osteoarthritis is a joint disorder, not a protein-deficiency disease.
Marasmus results from severe deficiency of energy and protein.
Colour blindness is usually an inherited condition, not a protein-deficiency disease.
Arteries generally do not have valves to prevent backward blood flow along their length.
Capillaries do not contain valves.
The rectum is part of the digestive system and does not contain blood-flow valves.
Veins contain valves that help prevent the backward flow of blood.
200–250 grams is generally below the typical adult heart-weight range.
150–200 grams is too low for a normal adult heart.
250–350 grams is the closest range for the weight of a normal adult heart.
100–200 grams is generally too low for a normal adult heart.
Volvox forms colonies of cells and has colonial organization.
Amoeba is a unicellular organism, not a colony.
A frog is a multicellular animal with organ-system organization.
Mustard is a multicellular plant with tissue and organ organization.
A good hypothesis should be consistent with available data.
A good hypothesis must be testable.
A hypothesis need not already be correct; it is tested to determine whether it is supported.
A good hypothesis should make predictions that can be tested.
In the five-kingdom classification, bacteria are not assigned to Protista.
In the five-kingdom classification, bacteria belong to Kingdom Monera.
Fungi are a separate kingdom and do not include bacteria.
Plantae consists of plants, not bacteria.
Chakor is a national bird of Pakistan, not its national animal.
Ibex is not the national animal of Pakistan.
Urial is not the national animal of Pakistan.
The markhor is the national animal of Pakistan.
Fungi generally have cell walls made mainly of chitin.
Algae generally have cell walls.
Animal cells do not have cell walls.
Plant cells generally have cell walls made mainly of cellulose.
Robert Hooke used a microscope to observe cork but did not develop the first microscope.
Zacharias Janssen is commonly credited with developing the first compound microscope.
Louis Pasteur was a microbiologist, not the developer of the first microscope.
Robert Brown discovered the cell nucleus, not the first microscope.
Spindle fibers form during prophase, before metaphase.
Interphase is when the cell grows and copies its DNA; the mitotic spindle forms later.
G-2 is part of interphase and precedes spindle formation in prophase.
Spindle fibers begin forming during prophase.
Enzymes are generally proteins made from amino acids.
Minerals are not the structural building blocks of enzymes.
Vitamins may assist enzyme activity but do not make up enzyme structure.
Fats are not the structural building blocks of most enzymes.
